key_insight: For molten LiF, machine-learned potentials improve melting-point predictions over classical models, while the out-of-the-box MACE foundation model accurately reproduces experimental shear viscosity.
engineering_relevance: Machine-learned potentials could improve molten-salt transport modeling by capturing collective momentum dynamics that classical fixed-charge models miss.
method: Run molecular dynamics with Buckingham and Born–Huggins–Mayer classical potentials.
Compare MACE-MP-0b3 (small) with a fine-tuned version.
Evaluate melting points, shear viscosity, microscopic structure, and transport dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental viscosity agreement for the foundation model comparable to polarizable potentials, with enhanced viscosity linked to more elastic long-wavelength collective motion.
watch_item: The foundation and fine-tuned models predict substantially different melting points, so fine-tuning should not be assumed to improve every property.
paper_title: Dynamics and transport in LiF using classical and machine learned interatomic potentials
